text: The Fu Hong monks chant scripture day and night under the guidance of their Abbot, sustaining the might of the Yaksha of Burning Karma with the power of their vows, so that he may consume all beings of wicked karma with his ceaseless wrath, fulfilling the long-held sorrowful wish of Cathay's people.
An object empowered by the vows of the Fu Hong monks, possessed of many inconceivable abilities.

In the age when the Dragon Emperor still walked the earth, he shaped countless terracotta figures from his most loyal soldiers, to accompany him in campaigns across the land.\\nAfter years of endless warfare, the terracotta figures inevitably grew worn and broken, and the heroic spirits within them scattered and dispersed. Some figures and spirits became tainted with malevolent energy, bringing calamity upon the land and harming its people for ages.\\nTo relieve this suffering, the Fu Hong monks gathered the fragments of these figures and the remnants of their spirits, forging several Vidyottama Terracottas, driven by the power of scriptural vows — to shatter the armies of Chaos on one hand, and to purge these vengeful spirits on the other.\\nYet such methods were ever considered inauspicious, and Cathay never favored them. Once the fighting settled, they were sealed away and forgotten, until Fu Yuanshan uncovered traces of the Vidyottama Terracottas' whereabouts in records of ancient battles, and sought audience with the Fu Hong Abbot, finally bringing them back into the world.
The Yaksha of Burning Karma ceaselessly shakes his vajra bell, crushing evil and impurity, cleansing malevolent miasma, and driving away demons.
Three thousand realms of dharma, all wicked sentient beings — swept away in an instant.
The Yaksha of Burning Karma gathers the vow-power of the Fu Hong monks, forging a dharma realm as unyielding as vajra.
The Yaksha of Burning Karma devours evil and purges impurity, forming a Garbha Realm around his body, its Wind of Magic steadfast and beyond the command of any enemy.

The pagoda atop the Great Bastion is a powerful shrine. It is said that the colossal sentinel of the wall dwells beside the tower, guarding the Great Bastion on one side while watching over the sealed Vidyottama Terracottas at the tower's base.\\nThe guards atop the Great Bastion can sometimes hear a deep, mighty roar rising from beneath the tower.
